The audit is complete. Here are the verified findings.

# Security audit: `/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-autoindex/src/extract/`

**Reachability chain (common to all findings).** Corpus files are read by `scan_file` (phase A, `lib.rs:2296`/`2446`, byte-limited) and by phase B at `lib.rs:7291` — `extract::extract(&f.path, &sn, None, &mut sink)` with `limit_bytes = None`, i.e. the whole file. Dispatch is `extract/mod.rs:191-242`. `sniff.rs:163` sets `sn.gzip` from the `1f 8b` magic, and `extract/mod.rs:114-128` (`open_reader`) wraps the file in `MultiGzDecoder` **with a `take(n)` cap only when `limit_bytes` is `Some`** — phase B passes `None`, so gzip decompression is unbounded for every streaming family. The size gate at `lib.rs:2341-2356` applies only to `Json | Html | Yaml | TxtProse | Pdf | Docx`; **Csv, Logs, SqlDump, Jsonl, Mbox, UnityYaml, Eml, Sqlite are exempt**. Input (file bytes and file name) is attacker-controlled; nothing below depends on operator config.

---

## HIGH 1 — csv_x.rs: unbounded single-record allocation + uncapped per-record field map (gzip bomb → OOM)

`/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-autoindex/src/extract/csv_x.rs`

```rust
21:    let mut rdr = csv::ReaderBuilder::new()
24:        .flexible(true)
25:        .from_reader(r);
...
53:        for (j, val) in rec.iter().enumerate() {
57:                format!("col_{}", j + 1)
```

The csv crate (1.4.0) has no record-size limit: `read_byte_record_impl` loops `OutputFull => { record.expand_fields(); continue; }` (verified in `~/.cargo/.../csv-1.4.0/src/reader.rs:1663`), so one row grows until its terminator. `csv_x.rs` reads through `open_reader(path, sn.gzip, limit_bytes)` — gzip-decompressed, uncapped in phase B — and then inserts every cell into a `Map` with **no `MAX_FIELDS_PER_RECORD` cap** (unlike `flatten_object`/`insert_field` elsewhere), minting up to millions of distinct `col_N` keys for one record.

**Empirically verified** with a replica of this exact reader construction: a **38,931-byte gzip** (40 MB decompressed: `id,v\n1,` + `"0," × 20,000,000`, no row terminator) produced one record with **20,000,002 fields** and **226 MB peak RSS** — a 5,800× on-disk-to-RSS amplification, scaling linearly (a ~1 MB gzip → ~6 GB decompressed → OOM kill of the whole run; `panic = "abort"` makes any downstream failure fatal too).

**Malicious input:** `bomb.csv.gz` containing `\xef\xbb\xbf`-free bytes `id,v\n1,` followed by `0,` repeated N times with no newline. The 8 KB sniff prefix sees a 2-line CSV with a header → `Family::Csv`, `gzip=true`.

---

## HIGH 2 — sqldump.rs: unbounded `values` Vec (16× byte amplification) and uncapped string accumulator inside one tuple

`/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-autoindex/src/extract/sqldump.rs`

```rust
207:                            values.push(Value::String(take_utf8(&mut sval)));
...
234:                                sval.push(b);
...
242:                        values.push(bare_value(&take_utf8(&mut sval)));
...
246:                        if sval.len() < HEAD_CAP {
247:                            sval.push(b);
```

Three problems in the streaming state machine:
- `values` is cleared only on `(` (line 151) and drained only at `)`. A tuple that never closes — `INSERT INTO t VALUES (0,0,0,…` with no `)` before EOF — pushes one `serde_json::Value` (32 B) per **2 decompressed bytes** (`0,`) → ~16× amplification of the decompressed stream, itself unbounded via gzip.
- The `St::Bare` arm caps `sval` at `HEAD_CAP` (lines 246-248) but the `St::InString` arm (lines 199-238) pushes every byte into `sval` with **no cap** — one unterminated `'…` string literal accumulates the entire remaining decompressed stream.
- `emit_tuple` (lines 312-325) inserts every value into `fields` with no field-count cap (`col_N` fallback names), same as HIGH 1.

**Malicious input:** `dump.sql.gz` decompressing to `SET NAMES x;INSERT INTO t VALUES (0,0,0,0,…` (never closed, no `;`, no `)`). The sniff prefix contains `INSERT INTO` and a `;` → `Family::SqlDump` (`sniff.rs:1373-1376`), `gzip=true`. A 100 KB gzip can expand past 100 GB.

---

## HIGH 3 — xml_x.rs: O(depth²) clone+join per start tag (CPU/memory hang from a few hundred KB)

`/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-autoindex/src/extract/xml_x.rs`

```rust
195:        let mut prefix_parts = st.stack.clone();
199:        let prefix = prefix_parts.join("_");
...
214:            st.root_stack[1..].to_vec()
221:        let prefix = parts.join("_");
```

Inside a captured record, **every** `Start`/`Empty` event clones the entire element stack (`Vec<String>`, one `String` per open element, pushed at line 193) and joins it — regardless of whether the element has attributes. With nesting depth D that is O(D) per event, O(D²) overall. quick-xml 0.41 is iterative with no depth limit, and the extraction loop has no event cap (the 4096-event cap applies only to `elect_record_tag`). Depth D is reachable because the election itself elects the repeated tag: `<a><a><a>…` gives `counts["a"] = (4095, structured=true)` (parents are marked structured at `xml_x.rs:334-338`) → `a` becomes `record_tag` → capture starts at the outermost `<a>` and every nested `<a>` pays the clone. A 600 KB file (`<a>` × 200k, unclosed) does ~2×10¹⁰ stack clones with average length 100k — effectively unbounded CPU plus gigabytes of transient allocation. The `record_tag == None` path (line 214, distinct nested tag names, no tag repeating ≥3×) is quadratic the same way and is even easier to hit. Secondary: `insert_field` (line 286) grows arrays without bound inside one record, and `st.stack`/`st.root_stack` grow ~13× the input bytes for deep nesting.

**Malicious input:** a plain `.xml` containing `<a>` repeated 200,000 times with no closing tags (or `<n0><n1><n2>…` with unique names for the root path).

---

## MEDIUM 4 — logs.rs: `lift_kv` builds an unbounded field map from one 16 MB line

`/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-autoindex/src/extract/logs.rs`

```rust
181:    let pairs: Vec<(String, String)> =
182:        t.kv.captures_iter(msg)
...
200:                m.entry(key).or_insert(Value::String(v));
```

`read_capped_line` caps a line at `MAX_LINE` (16 MB), but `lift_kv` collects every `key=value` pair into a `Vec` and then inserts each into the record's `Map` with **no field-count cap** — the `MAX_FIELDS_PER_RECORD` (512) cap that `json.rs`/`xml_x.rs`/`docx.rs` enforce is absent here. A 16 MB app/syslog line of `k0=1 k1=1 …` (5 bytes/pair, distinct keys) yields ~3.3 M pairs → Vec of tuples + per-pair heap Strings + BTreeMap nodes + `sanitize_field_name` clones ≈ **600 MB-1 GB transient RSS and seconds-to-minutes of CPU per line**, repeated for every matching line in the first 200 (election) and throughout phase B. Bounded by 16 MB × ~40×, but far outside the budget every sibling extractor enforces, and gzip-amplified (`Logs` is not size-gated).

**Malicious input:** `app.log.gz` decompressing to `2026-01-01 00:00:00,000 INFO k0=1 k1=1 k2=1 …` with distinct keys padding one line past 16 MB.

## MEDIUM 5 — txt.rs: line window retains up to 40 × 16 MB ≈ 640 MB

`/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-autoindex/src/extract/txt.rs`

```rust
91:    let mut window: Vec<(String, usize, u64)> = Vec::with_capacity(CHUNK_LINES);
163:        window.push((line.to_string(), line_no, start));
164:        if window.len() >= CHUNK_LINES && !flush(&mut window, false, &mut stats, sink) {
```

`read_capped_line` caps each line at `MAX_LINE` (16 MB) but `extract_lines` never skips over-cap lines (jsonl junk-counts them; txt keeps them). Up to `CHUNK_LINES` (40) lines are owned by `window` before `flush`, and `flush`'s 8 KB byte cap limits only the *emitted* text, not the window. Peak = 40 × ~16 MB ≈ **640 MB** from a single gzipped `.txt` whose decompressed payload is 40 newline-free 16 MB lines (~640 MB decompressed from a <1 MB gzip). Fixed ceiling, not unbounded — but well above the documented ~0.3 GB working set.

## LOW 6 — sqlite_x.rs: URI path escapes only `?`

`/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-autoindex/src/extract/sqlite_x.rs`

```rust
13:    let uri = format!(
14:        "file:{}?immutable=1&mode=ro",
15:        path.to_string_lossy().replace('?', "%3f")
```

SQLite URI filenames percent-decode and end at `#`; only `?` is escaped. A corpus-provided file *name* containing `%` sequences (decoded to a different, existing path) or `#` (query truncated, `immutable=1&mode=ro` can be dropped from the fragment boundary) can make rusqlite open a different file than the walker sniffed, or open it without `mode=ro`. Impact is limited (the decoded path must exist under the same tree, and no writes are issued), but the file name is attacker-controlled and the escaping is incomplete. Table-name interpolation is safe (`"`→`""` at line 32).

## LOW 7 — docx.rs: ~3× transient amplification of the 72 MB decompression cap

`/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-autoindex/src/extract/docx.rs` — lines 85 (`para` cap check), 107 (`body.push_str`), 122-124 (loop break). `para` (≤ ~72 MB) + `body` (≤ ~72 MB) + `headings` (clones, ≤ body) coexist → ~216 MB transient from a file whose decompressed stream is capped at 72 MB. Bounded and consistent with the codebase's stated budget (`MAX_EML` = 64 MB, `PDF_CAP` = 512 MB); noted only for completeness. Zip handling itself is safe: only `word/document.xml` is read via `by_name`, nothing is extracted to disk (no zip-slip), and decompression goes through `Read::take` (line 48).

---

## Checked and found safe (coverage notes)

- **pdf.rs**: parsing runs in a fresh worker process with `RLIMIT_AS` 1536 MB, a process group, and a timeout (`pdf.rs:1082-1099`, `936-1028`); parent-side response is capped at 32 MB (`read_capped`). A panic in `pdf_oxide` kills only the worker. `Arc::get_mut(...).expect` (line 321) and the `Mutex::lock().unwrap()`s are not input-reachable.
- **serde_yaml 0.9.34** enforces a 128-level recursion limit (`de.rs:112`, `recursion_check`), so deeply nested YAML cannot stack-overflow `yaml_to_json` (`mod.rs:309`, recursive but depth ≤ 128) or `unity.rs::collect_guid_refs`.
- **json.rs:78-79** `obj.remove(&key).unwrap()` / `unreachable!()` — `key` was just cloned out of the same `obj` (line 72) with no intervening mutation; genuinely unreachable. Whole-file read capped at 64 MB; serde_json's default 128-depth limit applies.
- **eml.rs / mbox.rs**: byte-oriented throughout; message offsets read via `.get(a..b)?` (`eml.rs:606-608`); per-message cap `MAX_EML` = 64 MB; process-wide 256 MB in-flight budget (`mbox.rs:484`); `truncate(len - strip)` and `&head[skip..]` are guarded by construction. PDF attachments are routed through the isolated worker via an anonymous tempfile (no attacker-influenced path).
- **html.rs / code.rs**: all slicing is ASCII-scan-derived on byte boundaries (`scan_tag`, `raw_text_end` use `bytes.get(...)`); `code.rs` uses fixed `read_whole` cap (2 MB) and static tree-sitter queries; `Query::new(...).unwrap_or_else(panic!)` (code.rs:55) uses compiled-in query strings, not file content.
- **Regexes**: all patterns are static constants (logs/sqldump/csv); the `regex` crate is linear-time, so no catastrophic backtracking; no pattern is built from file content.
- **sqldump multibyte slicing** (`head[..6]`, `trimmed[..12]`) — already converted to byte slices with `get(..12)`; the historical panics are fixed.
- No extraction-to-disk, no shell invocation, no path/script/config interpolation from document content anywhere in the dispatch tree (the only subprocess is the PDF worker with fixed argv).

The single systemic root cause behind HIGH 1/2 and MEDIUM 4/5: **streaming families get no cap on gzip-decompressed bytes and no per-record field-count cap** — adding a decoded-byte `take` in `open_reader` for full runs (or a record-size limit in csv/sqldump, plus `MAX_FIELDS_PER_RECORD` in csv/logs/sqldump) would close the whole class.
